title: Pointers to const and const Pointers
learningObjectives: Explain pointers to const and const pointers.
Describe pointer/reference or lifetime rules involved.
Trace a simple memory access or ownership operation.
Recognize common undefined behavior and safety risks.
Choose a safer approach for a practical task.

understand.concept: const T* prevents modifying the pointed-to T through that pointer; T* const prevents reassignment of the pointer itself. const T* const prevents both.
understand.whyItMatters: Const qualifiers make intent explicit and reduce accidental mutation.
understand.explain: Read const placement from right to left: what is const, pointer or pointed value?

examples.title: Pointer to const data
examples.code: int n=5;const int* p=&n;\n// *p=6 is not allowed
examples.explanation: The pointed value cannot be modified through p.

examples.title: Const pointer
examples.code: int a=1,b=2;int* const p=&a;\n*p=3; // allowed; p=&b is not
examples.explanation: The pointer itself cannot be reassigned after initialization.

examples.title: Both const
examples.code: int n=4;const int* const p=&n;\n// cannot reassign p or modify *p
examples.explanation: Both pointer and pointed value are const through this access.

examples.title: Read-only helper
examples.explanation: The function reads but cannot modify the pointed int.

examples.title: Qualifier interpretation
examples.code: const int* p; // pointer to const int\nint* const q=&n; // const pointer to int
examples.explanation: The placement of const changes what is protected.

practise.guidedTask: Trace the five Pointers to const and const Pointers examples. Mark each pointer/reference's target, object lifetime, mutability and whether dereferencing is valid.
practise.independentTask: Build a small C++ exercise showing pointers to const and const pointers. Include safe cases and deliberately describe (but do not execute) one invalid case. Demonstrate how ownership or lifetime is managed.
hints: Draw pointer arrows to live objects.
Use nullptr for empty pointers and check before dereferencing.
Keep pointer arithmetic within one array.
Distinguish pointer constness from pointee constness.
Prefer value returns, containers and smart pointers to manual ownership.
